items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: And the house band was John C. Smith. You know he had a sedate band.

ctx.x: Would you like to take that and put it behind you?

Yeah, yeah. That's a good idea, yeah. I was about -- put it like this. Yeah. Yeah. Nice. Thanks. At that time, you see, I had -- I never could remember whether this was before -- well, when I was about 14 or 15 years old I discovered Fletcher Henderson's band, because I went to a dance. Fletcher Henderson was playing at the Roseland Ballroom, Roseland Ballroom in New York, and so all these clubs, you know, these colored clubs, used to give these big dances and they used to give dances at the Renaissance Casino.…

stock arrangements, you know, till Fletcher got there, then he'd turn on the jazz. So anyhow, so you know, young kids, we went to this dance. It cost $1.10 to go to the dance. So we saved our money and we went to the dance.
